items.prompt: Even numbers can make pairs. Everyone gets a partner!
items.say: Even numbers can make pairs. Everyone gets a partner! 6 shoes make 3 pairs, so 6 is even.

items.prompt: Odd numbers always have one left over.
items.say: Odd numbers always have one left over. Look, one shoe has no partner. So 5 is odd.
items.text: One shoe has no partner. 5 is odd.

items.explain: 4 makes 2 pairs with none left over, so 4 is even.
7 makes 3 pairs and 1 is left over, so 7 is odd.
10 makes 5 pairs with none left over, so 10 is even.

items.prompt: Count by 2s to say the even numbers!
items.say: Count by twos: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. These are the even numbers. The numbers in between, 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, are odd.
items.text: The numbers in between are odd: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.

items.say: Count by twos. 2, 4, 6, what comes next?

items.explain: 9 always has one left over. 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 are odd.

items.say: Here is a big one. Is 13 even or odd?
items.explain: 13 makes 6 pairs and 1 is left over, so 13 is odd.

items.prompt: Count to 10 out loud. Clap on every even number!
items.say: Stand up! Count to 10 out loud, and clap on every even number: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10!

audio.t: Even numbers can make pairs. Everyone gets a partner! 6 shoes make 3 pairs, so 6 is even.

Not quite. 10 makes 5 pairs with none left over, so 10 is even.
Not quite. 2, 4, 6, 8. Each even number is 2 more.
Not quite. 9 always has one left over. 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 are odd.

Not quite. 13 makes 6 pairs and 1 is left over, so 13 is odd.
